short: ETV2 (ER71), ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are ETS-domain proteins that read the same GGA(A/T) core as the rest of the family. ETV2 is a transient activator required for the specification of blood and endothelium; ETV6 and ETV7 are repressors, and ETV6 spreads repression by polymerizing through its PNT/SAM domain. They are grouped here because their motif models cluster together, not because they share a distinct binding preference: ETV2's selected sequence is the ordinary class I ETS site and ETV6/ETV7 differ from it only marginally. What does recur among these models is arrangement - several are two GGAA cores in tandem or head-to-head. ETV6 is one of the most frequently rearranged genes in leukemia, most famously as ETV6-RUNX1 in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
long:
## The factors

Three genes sit in this family. ETV2 (also ER71 or ETSRP) is a transient transcriptional activator
expressed in a narrow window in nascent mesoderm and hemogenic endothelium and essentially silent
in adult tissues. ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are transcriptional repressors; ETV6 is broadly
expressed, ETV7 more narrowly and largely in hematopoietic cells. All three carry one ETS domain of
about 85 residues, the family's winged helix-turn-helix fold, and bind DNA as monomers. ETV6 and
ETV7 additionally carry a PNT domain (a SAM domain) that self-associates head-to-tail into an
open-ended polymer, so one DNA-bound ETV6 molecule can nucleate a long repressive assembly; the
polymer interface and its regulation have been mapped biophysically. ETV6 also has an
autoinhibitory element that damps its DNA binding. It is worth stating plainly that this family is
not a biochemical class. Systematic profiling of every human and mouse ETS protein put ETV6 and
ETV7 in a small subclass of their own (class IIb) and did not group ETV2 with them; ETV2's
preference is the ordinary class I preference.

## The motif

The consensus is ACCGGAAGT - the same nine-mer as ETS class I, read the same way, by two invariant
arginines in recognition helix H3 that hydrogen-bond the two guanines of GGA, with wing and turn
lysines contacting the flanks. The in vitro models differ only at the margins: JASPAR's HT-SELEX
model for ETV2 (MA0762.2) is ACCGGAAAT, with A rather than G immediately 3' of the core, while the
ETV6 (MA0645.2) and ETV7 (MA1708.2) HT-SELEX models are plain CCGGAAGT and CGGAAGTG. There is no
sequence that belongs to this family and not to ETS class I. What is distinctive in part of the
collection is arrangement rather than composition: three models here are doubled sites - CIS-BP
M02990 (CCGGAAGCGGAAGT), CIS-BP M04712 (CGGAAGTACTTCCG) and the ETV7 in vitro model
(CCCGGAAGTACTTC) - that is, two ETS cores in tandem or head-to-head. That is consistent with
ETV6's ability to polymerize and with the reported preference of these factors for repeated GGAA,
but doubled and repeated GGAA matrices also occur in ETS class I, where the EWS-FLI1 fusion's GGAA
microsatellite matrices live, so a tandem arrangement does not on its own assign a motif here.

## Where it acts

ETV2 binds enhancers of endothelial and hematopoietic genes during a short developmental window,
acting downstream of BMP, Notch and Wnt signals. ETV6 and ETV7 occupy ETS sites at promoters and
enhancers and repress them, recruiting corepressors rather than activating. The functional point
this family illustrates is competition: because ETV6, ETV7, ERF and ETV3 read the same sequence as
ETS1, ERG, FLI1 and GABPA, the output of a given ETS site depends on which family member happens to
occupy it, not on the sequence. That is also why sites bound by these repressors are not
distinguishable in a scan from sites bound by activators. Notably, the genome-wide footprint
archetypes derived from DNase data contain no archetype for this family: every archetype whose name
includes ETV clustered instead with ELF, ELK or ETS archetypes that are assigned elsewhere in this
atlas.

## Biology and disease

Etv2-null mouse embryos fail to make blood and endothelium, placing ETV2 at the top of the
hematoendothelial program; the gene is now widely used to force endothelial fate in reprogramming
experiments. Mice lacking Tel/Etv6 die around mid-gestation with a yolk sac angiogenic defect and
intra-embryonic apoptosis, and ETV6 is required for adult bone marrow hematopoiesis. ETV6 is among
the most frequently rearranged genes in human leukemia: the t(12;21) fusion ETV6-RUNX1 (TEL-AML1)
is the most common recurrent fusion in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and ETV6
has many other partners including kinases. Germline heterozygous ETV6 mutations cause autosomal
dominant thrombocytopenia with predisposition to hematologic malignancy.

## Reading a hit

This is the family in this atlas where the label deserves the least weight. The motifs assigned
here are not separable from ETS class I, and the data say so directly: for 15 of the 16 models in
this family, most of the nearest neighbours across the four databases are labelled with a different
family, usually ETS class I, and for 14 of them the single best match anywhere is a motif
rather than a motif from this family - including the CIS-BP model that this atlas picks as the
family's representative. One JASPAR entry, the heterodimer model ETV2::FIGLA (MA1941.2), is flagged
outright as belonging with class I. Practical consequences: read a hit as "an ETS site"; use
expression to decide the factor, remembering that ETV2 is effectively absent outside early mesoderm
and engineered endothelial systems, so an ETV2 call in an adult tissue dataset is far more likely a
generic ETS site; and do not try to tell ETV6 from ERF or ETV3, all repressors reading the same
sequence. Four of the seven JASPAR models here are CAP-SELEX heterodimers (ETV2::HOXB13,
ETV2::FIGLA, ETV2::DRGX, ETV2::FOXI1) in which much of the matrix is a HOX, bHLH or FOX site rather
than an ETS site.
caveats:
Treat the family label as provisional. Its separation from ETS class I is largely a
clustering outcome: 15 of 16 models here have most of their cross-database nearest neighbours
labelled with another family, usually class I, 14 match a motif outside the family better than any
inside it, and one JASPAR entry (ETV2::FIGLA) is flagged as belonging with class I. The published classification also does not support the grouping - ETV6 and ETV7
form their own small subclass while ETV2 behaves like a class I factor. No genomic-footprint
archetype corresponds to this family. Four of seven JASPAR models are CAP-SELEX heterodimers whose
matrices are partly a HOX, bHLH or FOX site. A hit therefore means "an ETS site"; which of ETV2,
ETV6, ETV7, ERF or ETV3 is bound has to come from expression and ChIP data.
